title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing ordering for partial JSON + delimiter edgecases
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: streaming SSE responses for chat/generation endpoints sometimes emitted token/event fragments in an ordering that caused partial JSON objects to be emitted with delimiters in the wrong order (e.g. trailing delimiter line arriving before final token payload). This caused client JSON parsers and the OpenAI-compatibility layer to mis-reconstruct structured output and function-calling payloads. Motivation: customer-reported regressions for structured-tool-calls and partial-json streaming clients (SUP-1123) and internal flaky e2e tests. This PR fixes framing/delimiter ordering and makes the streaming exit protocol deterministic. Summary of changes: 1) Ensure SSE event boundary ('data:' lines) are emitted after token payloads for partial-json cases by adjusting the chunk aggregator ordering. 2) Introduce an explicit "partial_json_state" in the streamer (in-memory flag) to avoid interleaving delimiter frames when prefix/kv cache flushes occur. 3) Add guards to avoid emitting empty 'data: [DONE]' events before the final token for race conditions between flush and stream-close. 4) Add integration tests that replay historical failing traces and a new deterministic SSE parser test. 5) Add compatibility shim in openai-compat layer to tolerate trailing newlines but log once if ordering is incorrect (helps gradual rollout). Checklist: - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Run benchmark canary for latency regression - [x] Add release note - [x] Add reviewer sign-offs Impact: fixes streaming-delimited partial JSON failures seen in function-calling and structured-output consumers. No API contract change for clients that follow SSE spec; improves robustness. Rollout: merged to main and will be cherry-picked to release/2026-02 in a follow-up. Related: ENG-4321, SUP-1123, previous PRs addressing similar issues (pr-95012, pr-91824).
